acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — Terraform provisions, per environment, an API Gateway HTTP API (payload format 2.0) integrated with a Lambda (nodejs24.x, not VPC-attached) whose IAM role grants only s3:PutObject on the event bucket ARN and ssm:GetParameter + kms:Decrypt on the webhook-secret parameter. No wildcard resource ARNs.

verification.definingInputProperty: A planned Lambda in each environment root
verification.assertions: Runtime is nodejs24.x; no vpc_config block is present

verification.definingInputProperty: Every IAM policy document in the module
verification.assertions: No wildcard resource ARN anywhere — the negative half of least-privilege

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — The endpoint is fronted by a CloudFront distribution with an AWS WAF Web ACL attached (Web ACL created in us-east-1 with scope = "CLOUDFRONT"), carrying the aws.md managed rule set — AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList — plus an explicit rate-limit rule. WAF logging is enabled to an S3 log destination with a 60-day expiry per aws.md.

verification.definingInputProperty: A deployed CloudFront distribution with the Web ACL associated, receiving real requests
verification.assertions: All four rules present via get-web-acl; a probe request matching a managed rule returns 403; a benign request is NOT blocked; the WAF log bucket receives a record and carries a 60-day expiry rule

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — The origin cannot be reached around the WAF. CloudFront injects a secret origin-verify header (value from SSM, never in Terraform state as plaintext); the Lambda rejects any request lacking the correct value with 403 before doing any other work. A direct POST to the raw https://{api-id}.execute-api.{region}.amazonaws.com/... URL therefore returns 403, not 404 or 200.

verification.definingInputProperty: A request sent to the raw execute-api URL, bypassing CloudFront entirely — not a CloudFront request with the header stripped
verification.assertions: Raw execute-api POST returns 403; the same path through CloudFront returns 404 (unregistered), proving the 403 originates from the origin check rather than the path being unroutable; logs record the rejection without echoing either secret value

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — A per-environment custom hostname resolves and serves the endpoint: hooks.dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com and hooks.prod.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, each backed by an ACM certificate in us-east-1 (CloudFront's requirement) validated by DNS records in that environment's own zone from AWE-151, with the alias A/AAAA record in the same zone.

verification.definingInputProperty: Public DNS resolution and a real TLS handshake, not a Route53 API listing
verification.assertions: The hostname resolves to the CloudFront distribution; HTTPS completes with a valid certificate; the unregistered path returns 404

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — A generic Lambda handler routes a request to a registered integration by path (e.g. /github), hands it the raw request (headers + raw body), and maps its outcome to an HTTP status. The handler is integration-agnostic: it contains no provider names, no signature verification, and no classification. This story ships the registry empty, so every POST to an unregistered path returns 404; GitHub registers itself in AWE-156.

verification.definingInputProperty: A stub WebhookIntegration returning each WebhookOutcome variant, plus an unregistered path
verification.assertions: Each outcome maps to its documented status; an unregistered path returns 404
No provider name or signature vocabulary appears — the integration-agnostic half of the criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — Persistence goes through the single existing Repository. The handler and its integrations obtain put from the EventRepository Context.Tag (@personal-events/core, AWE-153), provided by the S3EventRepositoryLayer from @personal-events/s3-repository (AWE-213). No new S3 write path, no new event-writing package, and no direct @aws-sdk/client-s3 use outside that layer.

verification.definingInputProperty: The whole ingest app and the packages directory
verification.assertions: No S3 SDK import in the app; no event-sink package exists — the static half

verification.definingInputProperty: A handler test providing a capturing EventRepository layer
verification.assertions: put/putAll is invoked through the tag — the behavioural half, which the static check alone cannot establish

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — Raw body integrity is preserved. The handler passes the exact request bytes through to the integration (base64-decoded only when isBase64Encoded is true), never JSON-parsing and re-serialising first, because AWE-156's HMAC signs the exact bytes. A test asserts a body with unusual-but-valid whitespace and Unicode survives byte-identical.

verification.definingInputProperty: A body containing significant whitespace, a trailing newline, multi-byte UTF-8, and key ordering that a re-serialisation round-trip would alter
verification.assertions: The bytes the stub integration receives are identical to the bytes sent, for both base64 and plain encodings

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — Effect throughout: every effectful function returns Effect; pure fallible helpers return Either; a raw Promise appears only in the exported Lambda handler, via Effect.runPromise (per CLAUDE.md).

verification.definingInputProperty: Every source module except the handler export

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-09 — Logging is Effect's Logger, not winston. Every record carries level, env, timestamp (ms), service (webhook-ingest) and the request id from event.requestContext.requestId, emitted as JSONL to the CloudWatch stream per .agents/guidance/logging.md. The webhook secret and the origin-verify value are never logged, at any level.

verification.definingInputProperty: A sentinel secret value injected, exercised across every failure path in the AC-11 inventory
verification.assertions: The captured log output contains the sentinel zero times; every emitted record is valid JSON carrying level, env, timestamp with ms, service and requestId

verification.definingInputProperty: The whole ingest app including package.json

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-10 — terraform fmt -check, validate and plan are clean for every environment root, and a second plan after apply reports no drift — including no perpetual diff on the CloudFront distribution or the WAF Web ACL.

verification.command: for d in development production; do terraform -chdir=infra/environments/$d plan -detailed-exitcode || exit 1; done
verification.definingInputProperty: A plan executed AFTER a completed apply, across the complete set of environment roots
verification.assertions: -detailed-exitcode returns 0 for every root; exit code 2 means drift and fails this criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-11 — Failure modes, each logged with the offending value and mapped to the right status: unroutable path → 404; missing/incorrect origin-verify header → 403; malformed request body → 400; S3 write failure → 5xx (so the sender can redeliver — GitHub does not auto-retry, making this load-bearing); missing SSM parameter → 5xx with a message naming the parameter; IAM denial → 5xx with the denied action and resource named.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete enumerated set of 7 failure cases, each carrying the property that triggers its specific mode
verification.assertions: Each case returns its exact documented status and logs the offending value; a guard asserts the table length equals 7 so the inventory cannot silently shrink

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-12 — Guidance conformance: G-C-P separation across distinct modules, Repository pattern (no SDK above the boundary), Record lookups rather than if/else if on a discriminator, no accumulator loops, no enums, explicit return types. Verified by biome + typecheck.

verification.command: pnpm --filter @personal-events/webhook-ingest exec biome check src && pnpm --filter @personal-events/webhook-ingest typecheck

verification.assertions: No TypeScript enum — a counterexample check biome does not enforce

tests.productionWriteApproval: REQUIRED AND NOT YET GRANTED. Distinct from the AWE-151/AWE-213 approvals granted 2026-08-31, which covered only minimal-event-pipeline resources. Ask at the start of github-integration execution: 'May I run terraform apply against account 269378281721 to create, per environment: an API Gateway HTTP API, a Lambda and its IAM role, a CloudFront distribution, a us-east-1 ACM certificate (with DNS-validation records in the AWE-151 environment zone), a WAF Web ACL with four rules, an SSM parameter holding the origin-verify secret, and a WAF log bucket? This creates a publicly reachable internet endpoint and adds roughly $10/month per environment in WAF charges. Rollback is terraform destroy; CloudFront distributions take 15-20 minutes to disable and delete.'

entryPoints.entryPoint: Raw execute-api origin URL (must be unusable)
